tested_law: On T2-O states, relative outcome code in GF(2)^2 equals a rank-phase offset XOR the fixed per-component values of all odd-multiplicity component types.

findings.statement: The direct two-bit affine XOR outcome code is inconsistent on every one of the eight complete T2-O carriers. This remains true when one independent affine offset is supplied for each rank-mod-3 phase.
A global no-phase affine valuation also fails on every carrier. Rank-mod-3 offsets reduce the contradiction count in some geometries but do not eliminate contradictions in any geometry.

The failed systems are strongly constrained rather than merely underdetermined: after elimination, active nullity is only 1 or 2 in every tested carrier, yet nonzero contradiction rows remain (from 6 contradictions on 3x3-k3 up to 3,160 on 4x4-k4).

This rejects the simplest stable per-component GF(2)^2 affine valuation with phase offsets. It does not reject the already-qualified parity-based Q-V quotient, an arbitrary decoder on that quotient, phase-dependent component valuations, higher-order component interactions, or a different finite algebra.

Because the component carrier is scheduler-graded, the next linear test should allow the component valuation itself to depend on the rank phase, g_{G,r3}(C), rather than changing only a global phase offset. If that also fails, independent linear component valuation is rejected within fixed phase.

The negative affine result does not alter Q-V sufficiency of (M2, rank mod 3, T2): a finite exact decoder exists on the tested carriers by the prior collision audit, but that decoder is not this simplest affine XOR code.

next_question: Does the T2-O Q-V map become affine XOR when component values are graded by rank mod 3, or do same-phase contradictions force nonlinear/interacting component valuation?
